mainTopic: A conditional נידוי learned from יהודה; then the laws of the עיר מקלט and how the כהן גדול's death, or his unfitness, ends the killer's exile.
overview: רב teaches that a נידוי declared on a condition must still be formally undone, even if the condition never happens. The גמרא learns this from יהודה. His bones rattled in his coffin for forty years in the מדבר, even though he had brought בנימין back, until משה prayed for him. Each phrase of יהודה's ברכה fixed another problem. The גמרא then asks whether the accidental killer goes home only when all the listed כהנים גדולים die, or when just one does, and an attempted proof is pushed aside. A new משנה teaches that the timing of the כהן גדול's death decides the exile. It also says the killer may never leave the עיר מקלט, not even to testify or lead the army, and that the city's תחום protects him like the city itself. The גמרא explains these rules: a קל וחומר from אביי, a פסוק about the כהן גדול 'anointed in his days', and burial rules for a killer who dies. Finally, רבי אמי and רבי יצחק נפחא argue about a כהן גדול found to be unfit, and the גמרא suggests their argument matches that of רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע. That suggestion is tested on the next amud.

steps.title: A conditional ban must be formally undone
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that a נידוי declared on a condition needs a הפרה (annulment).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: a ban declared on a condition still needs to be undone.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new rule: if someone declares a נידוי 'on condition,' the ban needs to be formally cancelled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think a conditional ban only matters if the condition happens. רב says no. Once the words of נידוי are spoken, they carry weight and must be actively undone with a הפרה.

keyTerms.meaning: A ban; a person is set apart as a sinner

steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that spoken words of a ban are serious, even when they are wrapped in a condition.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
A ban made on a condition requires annulment.

steps.title: What is the source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where רב's rule comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source for רב's rule. This sets up the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a standard request for a source, not an attack. The גמרא wants a פסוק or story that shows a conditional ban still has power.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know it?

phrases.english: From where do we derive this?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for the rule that a conditional נידוי needs הפרה.

steps.title: The source is יהודה's promise to יעקב
steps.stepSummary: יהודה promised: if I don't bring בנימין back, I will be a sinner forever. That was a conditional ban on himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learn it from יהודה, as it is written: 'If I do not bring him back to you, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the source is יהודה. He put a conditional ban on himself to convince יעקב to let בנימין go down to מצרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rest of the פסוק reads 'I will be a sinner to you all the days,' which is a self-imposed ban. יהודה did bring בנימין back, so the condition never happened. The next steps show that the ban still affected him.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Etc.' The rest of the פסוק is assumed

phrases.english: From Judah, as it is written:
"If I do not bring him to you, etc."
phrases.notes: בראשית 43:9. The 'etc.' hides the key words: 'I will be a sinner to you all the days.'

steps.title: Why is יהודה's ברכה placed next to ראובן's?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יונתן asks what the link is between 'Let ראובן live' and 'And this for יהודה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יונתן: what is meant by 'Let ראובן live and not die… And this for יהודה'?
steps.whatsHappening: To show that יהודה's ban really hurt him, the גמרא brings a teaching that starts with a question about the order of משה's ברכות. This sets up the story in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In משה's ברכות, יהודה's ברכה comes right after ראובן's and begins with 'And this,' as if the two are connected. רבי יונתן wants to explain that connection.

keyTerms.meaning: What is meant by what is written?
'And this for יהודה,' the start of his ברכה

phrases.english: And Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani said
that Rabbi Yonatan said:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
"Let Reuben live and not die, etc."
phrases.notes: דברים 33:6

phrases.english: "And this for Judah"?
phrases.notes: דברים 33:7, the very next פסוק.

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why יהודה's ברכה is linked to ראובן's.

steps.title: יהודה's bones rattled until משה prayed
steps.stepSummary: For forty years יהודה's bones rattled in his coffin. Then משה prayed, pointing out that יהודה led ראובן to confess.
steps.simpleTranslation: All forty years that ישראל was in the מדבר, יהודה's bones rolled around in his coffin. Then משה prayed for him: 'Master of the World, who caused ראובן to confess? יהודה! Hear, ה׳, the voice of יהודה.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the proof. Even though יהודה brought בנימין back, his conditional ban still hurt him after death, until משה prayed for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rattling bones show the ban was still active, because no one had undone it. That proves רב's rule that a conditional ban needs a הפרה. It also explains the link: יהודה's admission led ראובן to admit his own sin, so יהודה deserves a ברכה right after ראובן.
steps.confusionAlert: יהודה did keep his promise and brought בנימין back. That is exactly the point: the ban's condition never happened, yet it still needed to be undone.

phrases.english: All those forty years
that Israel was in the wilderness,
the bones of Judah
were rolling around in the coffin,
phrases.notes: The people carried the bones of the שבטים out of מצרים with them.

phrases.english: until Moses stood up
and asked for mercy for him.
He said before Him: Master of the Universe,
who caused Reuben to confess? Judah!
"And this for Judah...
Hear, O Lord, the voice of Judah."
phrases.notes: דברים 33:7

steps.raayaObject: רב's rule that a conditional נידוי needs הפרה
steps.raayaSupportSource: יהודה's restless bones until משה's prayer, although he had fulfilled his condition

steps.title: Each phrase of the ברכה fixed another problem
steps.stepSummary: After the bones settled, יהודה still faced more problems, and משה's prayer fixed each one with another phrase of the ברכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: His limbs went back into place, but he was not let into the Heavenly ישיבה. So משה said, 'And bring him to his people.' He did not know how to discuss Torah with the רבנן, so משה said, 'His hands shall fight for him.' He could not answer a question, so משה said, 'And You shall help him against his enemies.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. Each phrase of יהודה's ברכה is read as a further request by משה, fixing one more effect of the ban.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban had several layers: his body was disturbed, he was kept out of the Heavenly ישיבה, and he could not discuss Torah or answer challenges there. Each layer needed its own prayer. This shows how fully a נידוי that was never undone stays in effect.
steps.whatToRemember: A נידוי said on a condition must still be formally undone. יהודה kept his word, yet his self-ban stayed in effect until משה prayed for him.

phrases.english: His limbs entered their place,
but they would not let him enter
into the heavenly academy;
"And bring him to his people."
phrases.notes: דברים 33:7. משה is asking that יהודה be let in.

phrases.english: He did not know how
to engage in give-and-take in halakha
with the Rabbis;
"His hands shall contend for him."
He did not know how to resolve a difficulty;
"And You shall be a help against his adversaries."

steps.raayaObject: How completely an unannulled conditional נידוי stays in force

steps.title: Does the killer go home at the death of all the כהנים גדולים, or of one?
steps.stepSummary: Back to the משנה: the גמרא asks whether the accidental killer goes home only when all the listed כהנים גדולים die, or when any one of them dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: does he go home only when all of them die, or maybe when one of them dies?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the יהודה story and returns to the משנה. It asks a new question about the רוצח בשוגג in the עיר מקלט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists several kinds of כהן גדול whose death lets the killer return home. If several are alive at once, it is unclear whether he must wait for all of them to die or only for the first one.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them (an open dilemma)
Returns home from the עיר מקלט

phrases.english: A dilemma was raised before them:
Is it with the death of all of them that he returns,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the accidental killer; 'them' are the כהנים גדולים listed in the משנה.

phrases.english: or perhaps with the death of one of them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the aside about נידוי and returns to the משנה about the עיר מקלט.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the death of one listed כהן גדול is enough for the killer's release, or all must die.

steps.title: Trying to answer from the next משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the משנה that says if there was no כהן גדול at the verdict, the killer never leaves. If any one of the listed כהנים frees him, he should be able to go free when one of those others dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if his verdict was decided when there was no כהן גדול, he never leaves the city. But if any one of them frees him, let him go home when one of these other כהנים dies!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer the question from step 7 by bringing a line from the upcoming משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier משנה listed other kinds of כהן גדול: one made כהן גדול only by wearing the special garments, and one who stepped down. If the death of any one of them frees the killer, then even when there is no serving כהן גדול, one of these others could free him. Yet the משנה says he never leaves, so it looks like these others do not count by themselves.

keyTerms.meaning: His verdict was decided; the moment he is sentenced to exile
The High Priest, whose death ends the exile
And if it is so; it sets up a contradiction with the opposite idea

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע: נִגְמַר דִּינוֹ בְּלֹא כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל –
phrases.english: Come and hear: if his verdict was decided without a High Priest
he never leaves there.
And if it is so,
phrases.notes: He means: if the death of any single one of the listed כהנים frees the killer.

phrases.english: let him return with one of these!
phrases.notes: 'These' are the other kinds of כהן גדול from the earlier משנה: one made כהן גדול by wearing the garments, and one who stepped down.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: נִגְמַר דִּינוֹ בְּלֹא כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attempts to answer the question from step 7
steps.raayaObject: Whether the death of any one listed כהן גדול frees the killer
steps.raayaSupportSource: The upcoming משנה: נגמר דינו בלא כהן גדול אינו יוצא משם לעולם

steps.title: The case is when none of them exist
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed aside: the משנה is talking about a time when there were no כהנים גדולים of any kind.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה means a case where there are none of these כהנים at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from step 8 with one word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Without a כהן גדול" can mean that no kind of כהן גדול was alive, not even a stepped-down one. So the משנה proves nothing about whether one of them alone would free the killer. The question from step 7 stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: In a case where there are none

phrases.english: Where there are none.
phrases.notes: None of the kinds of כהן גדול are alive at all, so there is no one whose death could free him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in step 8
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה can be read as a case where no כהן גדול of any kind exists
steps.whatToRemember: The question of whether all of the כהנים or any one of them must die is not settled by this משנה.

steps.title: When the timing of the כהן גדול's death matters
steps.stepSummary: If the כהן גדול dies after the verdict, the killer is not exiled. If a new כהן גדול was appointed before the verdict, the new one's death frees him. In three cases he never leaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the כהן גדול died after the verdict, the killer does not go into exile. If he died before the verdict and another was appointed, the killer goes home when the second one dies. If there was no כהן גדול at the verdict, or the killer killed a כהן גדול, or a כהן גדול was the killer, he never leaves.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins and explains how the timing of the כהן גדול's death affects the exile.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The exile is tied to the כהן גדול serving at the time of the verdict. If that כהן גדול is already gone when the verdict is given, the next one counts. In the three last cases there is no כהן גדול whose death can end the exile, so the exile lasts forever.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; a new משנה starts here
Goes into exile in an עיר מקלט
They appointed another in his place

phrases.english: MISHNA:
If after his verdict was decided the High Priest died
he is not exiled.
If before his verdict was decided

phrases.aramaic: מֵת כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל וּמִינּוּ אַחֵר תַּחְתָּיו
phrases.english: the High Priest died and they appointed another in his place
and afterward his verdict was decided
he returns with the death of the second.
If his verdict was decided without a High Priest,
and one who killed a High Priest,
and a High Priest who killed
never leaves there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה begins after the discussion of the previous one
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The exile depends on the כהן גדול at the time of the verdict; without one, or when a כהן גדול is the victim or the killer, the exile is permanent.
steps.confusionAlert: This is the same line the גמרא quoted in step 8. There it was used as a proof; here it is the משנה itself.

steps.title: He may never leave, even for testimony or the army
steps.stepSummary: The killer may not leave the city to testify in any kind of case, or even if the nation needs him as a general like יואב. The פסוק "אשר נס שמה" teaches that he lives, dies and is buried there.
steps.simpleTranslation: He does not leave, not to testify about a מצוה, about money, or in a death-penalty case. Even if the Jewish people need him, even if he is a general like יואב בן צרויה, he never leaves, because the פסוק says "that he fled there." There he lives, there he dies, there he is buried.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues and says the exile has no exceptions, and it brings a פסוק as its source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list goes from small needs to huge ones. Even life-and-death testimony, or the nation's need for its army general, does not let him out. The word "there" in the פסוק is read as covering his whole life: home, death and burial.

phrases.english: And he does not leave, not for testimony about a מצוה,
nor for testimony about money,
nor for testimony in capital cases.
And even if the Jewish people need him,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲפִילּוּ שַׂר צָבָא יִשְׂרָאֵל כְּיוֹאָב בֶּן צְרוּיָה
phrases.english: and even if he is the general of Israel's army, like Joab son of Zeruiah,
he never leaves there,
as it says: "that he fled there" —
phrases.notes: במדבר 35:25

phrases.english: there shall be his dwelling,

phrases.aramaic: שָׁם תְּהֵא מִיתָתוֹ, שָׁם תְּהֵא קְבוּרָתוֹ.
phrases.english: there shall be his death, there shall be his burial.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה, explaining what "never leaves" means in practice
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The גולה may not leave the עיר מקלט for any reason, not even to testify or to serve the nation.
steps.whatToRemember: "Never leaves" is absolute: from the word "there" (שמה) we learn he lives, dies and is buried in the עיר מקלט.

steps.title: The city's boundary protects like the city
steps.stepSummary: The area around the עיר מקלט, its תחום, protects the killer just like the city itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Just as the city protects him, so does its boundary area protect him.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a new rule: the protection reaches beyond the city walls to the surrounding boundary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being inside the walls is not required. Once he is inside the city's תחום, the גואל הדם may not touch him. This sets up the next question: what happens if he goes past that boundary.

keyTerms.meaning: Takes in and protects the killer
Its boundary area around the city

phrases.english: Just as the city takes him in,
so its boundary takes him in.
phrases.notes: The boundary is the area around the city, up to its שבת limit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with the area of protection
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תחום of the עיר מקלט gives the same protection as the city.

steps.title: If the killer steps outside the boundary
steps.stepSummary: If the killer leaves the תחום and the גואל הדם finds him, רבי יוסי הגלילי says killing him is a מצוה for the גואל הדם and permitted for anyone. רבי עקיבא says it is only permitted for the גואל הדם, and anyone else is held liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: A killer who went past the boundary and the גואל הדם found him: רבי יוסי הגלילי says it is a מצוה for the גואל הדם to kill him and allowed for anyone else. רבי עקיבא says it is only allowed for the גואל הדם, and anyone else who kills him is held liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a מחלוקת about a killer who left the protected area.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree he has lost his protection outside the boundary. They argue about how strong the permission is. For רבי יוסי הגלילי it is a מצוה for the גואל הדם and anyone may do it. For רבי עקיבא only the גואל הדם may do it, and a stranger who kills him is liable.

keyTerms.meaning: The relative of the victim who may avenge the death

phrases.english: A killer who went out beyond the boundary
and the blood redeemer found him,
Rabbi Yosei HaGelili says:
it is a מצוה for the blood redeemer,
and permitted for any person.
Rabbi Akiva says:
it is permitted for the blood redeemer,
and every other person is liable for him.

steps.triggerLanguage: רוֹצֵחַ שֶׁיֵּצֵא חוּץ לַתְּחוּם וּמְצָאוֹ גּוֹאֵל הַדָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the boundary rule: what happens past that boundary
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Outside the תחום the killer loses his protection. The two תנאים argue whether killing him is a מצוה for the גואל הדם and permitted for all, or only permitted for the גואל הדם.
steps.whatToRemember: Inside the city or its תחום he is safe. Outside it, רבי יוסי הגלילי and רבי עקיבא argue about who may kill him and how strong that permission is.

steps.title: Why is the killer not exiled if the כהן גדול died after the verdict?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking for the reason behind the משנה's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: What is the reason for the rule that he is not exiled?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by asking for the source of the משנה's rule: if the כהן גדול dies after the verdict, the killer does not go into exile. This question sets up אביי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave the rule but no reason. Normally a killer goes to the עיר מקלט once he is sentenced, so we need to know why the כהן גדול's death cancels that.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: He is asking about the משנה's rule: the כהן גדול died after the verdict, so the killer is not exiled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the first rule of the משנה quoted in step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason a killer is not exiled when the כהן גדול dies after his verdict.

steps.title: אביי's a fortiori argument
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues: if the כהן גדול's death frees someone already in exile, it should surely keep someone not yet exiled from going.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי says: it comes from a קל וחומר. If someone who was already exiled now goes free, then someone who was not yet exiled should certainly not be exiled.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers with a קל וחומר, an argument that moves from a weaker case to a stronger one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We know the כהן גדול's death releases a killer who is already in the עיר מקלט. A killer who has not even gone yet is in an easier position, so the same death should stop him from going at all.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a weaker case to a stronger one

phrases.english: Abaye said: It is a kal vachomer,
if one who was already exiled
now goes out,
then one who was not exiled,
is it not logical that he should not be exiled?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A קל וחומר from the killer already in exile, who is released by the כהן גדול's death.

steps.title: Maybe exile itself is what atones
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the קל וחומר: the exiled killer may go free because his exile already atoned for him, which is not true of the one who never went.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps the one who was exiled has already been atoned for, and the one who was not exiled has not!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks אביי's קל וחומר by pointing to a possible difference between the two killers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר only works if the 'easier' case really is easier. Here the exiled killer has something the other lacks: time served in exile. If exile is what brings כפרה, the killer who never went has earned nothing, so the proof falls apart.

phrases.english: But perhaps this one who was exiled has been atoned for,
but that one who was not exiled has not!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the קל וחומר of step 15.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The two cases may differ, because the exiled killer may have earned כפרה through his exile.

steps.title: The כהן גדול's death is what atones
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that exile does not bring כפרה. The death of the כהן גדול does, so the קל וחומר stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it exile that atones? It is the death of the כהן גדול that atones!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the challenge and saves אביי's proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the כפרה comes from the כהן גדול's death and not from time in exile, both killers are in the same position once he dies. That makes the קל וחומר work again.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it really...? (opens a question meant to reject)
The death of the כהן גדול

steps.whatToRemember: A killer sentenced to exile goes free once the כהן גדול dies, even if he never went, because the death of the כהן גדול is what brings the כפרה.

phrases.english: Is it exile that atones?
It is the death of the priest that atones!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the challenge of step 16 and confirms step 15.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Exile itself may be what atones.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the death of the כהן גדול atones, so the קל וחומר holds.

steps.title: Source for a כהן גדול appointed before the verdict
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה and asks where it comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: if before his verdict was decided, and so on. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next rule of the משנה and asks for its source. This sets up רב כהנא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that if a new כהן גדול was appointed before the verdict, the killer is freed by the new one's death. That seems strange, because the new כהן גדול was not in office when the killing happened.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know these things?

phrases.aramaic: אִם עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִגְמַר דִּינוֹ וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: If before his verdict was decided, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה: the כהן גדול died, a new one was appointed, and only then came the verdict.

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the second rule from step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source showing that a כהן גדול appointed after the killing but before the verdict counts.

steps.title: רב כהנא: the priest anointed in his days
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא reads the פסוק as speaking about a כהן גדול anointed during the killer's time, after the killing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: the פסוק says, 'He shall live there until the death of the כהן גדול whom he anointed with the holy oil.' Did the killer anoint him? Rather, it means the one who was anointed in his days.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא gives the source: a פסוק whose wording sounds strange if read literally.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read word for word, 'whom he anointed' sounds as if the killer anointed the כהן גדול, which cannot be right. So it must mean a כהן גדול anointed during the killer's days, after the killing. That includes one appointed before the verdict.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said: Because the verse says:
"And he shall dwell there until the death of the High Priest
phrases.notes: במדבר 35:25

phrases.english: whom he anointed with the holy oil,"
Now does he (the killer) anoint him?
Rather, this is the one who was anointed in his days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 18 with a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'whom he anointed' mean a כהן גדול anointed during the killer's days.

steps.title: What could the new כהן גדול have done?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the new כהן גדול is involved at all, since he could not have prevented the killing.
steps.simpleTranslation: What could he have done?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that the new כהן גדול's life should hold the killer in exile.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The killer's exile is tied to the כהן גדול because the כהן גדול shares some blame for not praying for his generation. A כהן גדול appointed after the killing could not have prayed to stop it, so why should his death matter?

phrases.english: What should he have done?
phrases.notes: Back on 11a we learned the כהן גדול shares the blame because he should have prayed. This one wasn't even in office yet!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the logic behind רב כהנא's rule in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: Linking the killer to a כהן גדול appointed after the killing
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The new כהן גדול had no chance to pray to prevent the killing, so he carries no blame.

steps.title: He should have prayed for a favorable verdict
steps.stepSummary: The new כהן גדול could have prayed that the killer be found innocent, and he did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: He should have asked for mercy that the killer's verdict end in his favor, and he did not ask.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the new כהן גדול did have something to pray for: the outcome of the trial.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the killing had already happened, the trial was still going on. The new כהן גדול could have prayed for an acquittal. Because he did not, he shares the blame, and his death frees the killer.

phrases.english: He should have asked for mercy
that his verdict would end favorably,
and he did not ask.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The new כהן גדול could have done nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: He could have prayed for an acquittal and did not, so he shares the blame.

steps.title: A killer who died before exile is buried in the עיר מקלט
steps.stepSummary: אביי reports a tradition: if the killer was sentenced and died, his bones are brought to the עיר מקלט, based on a פסוק about 'dwelling in the land.'
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: we have a tradition that if his verdict was decided and he died, his bones are brought there. The פסוק says 'to return to dwell in the land until the death of the כהן.' What kind of dwelling is in the land? That is burial.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי starts a new topic: what happens to a killer who was sentenced but died before he went to the עיר מקלט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks of dwelling 'in the land.' אביי reads 'in the land' as 'inside the ground,' which means burial. So even in death, the killer has to 'dwell' in the עיר מקלט until the כהן גדול dies.

keyTerms.meaning: We hold, we have a tradition

phrases.english: Abaye said: We have a tradition:
If his verdict was decided and he died,
they bring his bones there,
phrases.notes: "There" means the עיר מקלט he was sentenced to.

phrases.english: as it is written: "To return to dwell in the land
phrases.notes: במדבר 35:32

phrases.english: until the death of the priest,"
And what is a dwelling that is in the land?
You must say this is burial.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about a killer who dies, close to step 11's idea that he is buried in the city.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sentenced killer who died before going into exile is buried in the עיר מקלט.

steps.title: A killer who died in exile is later reburied with his ancestors
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that if the killer died before the כהן גדול, his bones are later moved to his family graves, since 'return to his ancestral land' means burial.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא taught: if he died before the כהן גדול died, his bones are brought to his ancestors' graves. The פסוק says 'the killer shall return to the land of his inheritance.' What kind of dwelling is in his ancestral land? That is burial.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא gives the other side of אביי's rule: what happens to a killer who died while still in exile.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using the same reading of 'dwelling' as burial, the ברייתא says the killer's return home also applies after death. Once the כהן גדול dies, his bones are moved to his family's burial place.

keyTerms.meaning: The land of his family inheritance

steps.whatToRemember: The killer's 'dwelling' applies to burial too. If he dies before going into exile, he is buried in the עיר מקלט. If he dies in exile, his bones go home to his family's graves after the כהן גדול dies.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנָא: מֵת קוֹדֶם שֶׁמֵּת כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל,
phrases.english: It was taught: If he died before the High Priest died,
they bring his bones to the graves of his ancestors,
phrases.notes: This happens once the כהן גדול dies, just as a living killer would go home then.

phrases.english: as it is written: "The killer shall return to the land of his inheritance,"
phrases.notes: במדבר 35:28

phrases.english: What is a dwelling that is in the land of his inheritance?
You must say this is burial.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: מֵת קוֹדֶם שֶׁמֵּת כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the matching case to אביי's rule in step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A killer who died in the עיר מקלט before the כהן גדול is reburied with his ancestors after the כהן גדול dies.

steps.title: Two views when the כהן גדול turns out to be unfit
steps.stepSummary: After the killer is sentenced, the כהן גדול is discovered to be a בן גרושה or בן חלוצה. רבי אמי and רבי יצחק נפחא disagree. One says the כהונה 'died'. The other says the כהונה is 'voided'.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the killer's verdict was decided, and then the כהן was found to be the son of a divorced woman or of a חלוצה, רבי אמי and רבי יצחק נפחא disagree. One says: the כהונה died. The other says: the כהונה is voided.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new case about exile: the כהן גדול turns out to be unfit for כהונה, and two אמוראים argue about what that means for the killer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'The כהונה died' means it is like the כהן גדול's death, so the killer may go home. 'The כהונה is voided' means it is as if there was no כהן גדול when the killer was sentenced, so there is no death that can ever free him. The question is whether the discovery works from now on, or erases his כהונה back to the start.

keyTerms.meaning: His verdict was decided (the killer was sentenced to exile)
Son of a divorced woman married to a כהן; he is a חלל and unfit for כהונה
Son of a woman who had חליצה, married to a כהן; also unfit for כהונה
The כהונה 'died': treated like the כהן גדול's death, from now on
The כהונה is voided: as if it never existed

steps.confusionAlert: 'Voided' does not help the killer. If there was never a real כהן גדול, there is no death that can free him.

phrases.english: His verdict was decided,
and the כהן became the son of a divorced woman
phrases.notes: 'Became' here means he was found out to be one; he was really born that way all along.

phrases.english: or the son of a חלוצה,

phrases.aramaic: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי יִצְחָק נַפָּחָא.
phrases.english: Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Yitzchak Nappacha disagree about it.
One says: the כהונה died.
And one says: the כהונה is voided.

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַבִּי אַמֵּי וְרַבִּי יִצְחָק נַפָּחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from where the killer is buried to a new case: a כהן גדול found to be unfit after the sentence.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a מחלוקת: either the unfit כהן גדול's כהונה 'died', which frees the killer, or it is 'voided', as if it never existed.

steps.title: Suggesting the argument matches רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the two אמוראים are repeating an older מחלוקת. A כהן was offering on the מזבח and was found to be a בן גרושה or בן חלוצה. רבי אליעזר says all his past offerings are invalid; רבי יהושע says they are valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say they argue in the same dispute as רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע? As we learned: if a כהן was standing and offering on the מזבח, and it became known he is a בן גרושה or בן חלוצה, רבי אליעזר says all the offerings he brought are invalid, and רבי יהושע says they are valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proposes that the new מחלוקת is really an older one, and quotes the משנה it has in mind. This sets up the next step, where it will match up who holds like whom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר treats the discovery as cancelling the כהן's status from the very start, so his past work is invalid. רבי יהושע treats him as a valid כהן until the moment it became known. This is the same 'from the start or from now on' question as 'voided' versus 'died'.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Shall we say': the גמרא offers a suggestion that it may later test

steps.confusionAlert: Both רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע agree he may not keep serving once it is known. They only argue about the offerings he already brought.

phrases.english: Shall we say that in the dispute

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ קָא מִיפַּלְגִי.
phrases.english: of Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua they are disagreeing?
As we learned: if he was standing and offering
phrases.notes: תרומות 8:1.

phrases.english: on top of the altar,
and it became known that he is the son of a divorced woman
or the son of a חלוצה,
Rabbi Eliezer says:
all the offerings that he brought are invalid,
and Rabbi Yehoshua declares them valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא בִּפְלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ קָא מִיפַּלְגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to link the אמוראים' מחלוקת from step 24 to an earlier תנאים dispute.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the dispute of רבי אמי and רבי יצחק נפחא the same as the dispute of רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע about an unfit כהן's past offerings?

steps.title: Matching each view to a תנא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out the match. 'The כהונה died' fits רבי יהושע, because the unfitness counts only from now on. 'The כהונה is voided' fits רבי אליעזר, because it is cancelled from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says 'it died' holds like רבי יהושע, and the one who says 'it is voided' holds like רבי אליעזר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its suggestion by pairing each אמורא's view with one of the תנאים. It is still asking, not deciding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע keeps the past offerings valid, so the כהן was a real כהן until now. That is why the discovery is like a 'death' that frees the killer. רבי אליעזר cancels everything from the start, so there was never a real כהן גדול, which matches 'voided'.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who says (the holder of a given opinion)

steps.whyThisMatters: If this match is right, the אמוראים would have nothing new to argue about. They would simply be taking sides in an older מחלוקת. The question mark means the גמרא is still testing whether the match is correct.

phrases.english: The one who says it 'died'
holds like Rabbi Yehoshua,
and the one who says it is 'voided'
holds like Rabbi Eliezer?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the 'לימא' suggestion of step 25 by pairing each view with a תנא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does 'died' match רבי יהושע and 'voided' match רבי אליעזר?
